title: Stack
summary: A vertical column of children with even spacing is the standard Column with verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy and a step of the Monarch space scale. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For any column of elements with even gaps: a form, the body of a card, a settings group. Pass MonarchTheme.spacing.space2, space4 and so on, never a number.
whenNotToUse: For a long or unbounded list use a LazyColumn with verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy. For a horizontal row that wraps use FlowRow (see inline).
api: @Composable inline fun Column(modifier: Modifier = Modifier, verticalArrangement: Arrangement.Vertical = Arrangement.Top, horizontalAlignment: Alignment.Horizontal = Alignment.Start, content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)
appearance: No appearance of its own; the gaps are steps of the space scale. Dividers between children are MonarchDivider.
platformNotes: The web Stack has gap, align, justify, dividers and an element name. On Android gap is Arrangement.spacedBy with a value from MonarchTheme.spacing, align is horizontalAlignment (Alignment.Start, CenterHorizontally, End, which mirror in right to left), and justify is the alignment argument of spacedBy or Arrangement.SpaceBetween. dividers is a MonarchDivider written between the children. Stretching children to the full width is fillMaxWidth() on each child. The element name has no meaning: semantics are set on the children. iOS uses VStack with spacing.
accessibility: No behavior of its own: TalkBack reads the children in order.
edgeCases: spacedBy adds no space before the first or after the last child; use padding for outer space.
